items.title: Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts
items.content: Cyber experts say AI labs’ containment and monitoring failures — not agents with minds of their own — are to blame for recent alarming hacking reports. CISOs should vet their AI vendors and tighten security basics as safeguards.
items.author: latexr
items.summary_zh: 网络安全专家认为，近期一批被渲染成 AI 自主攻击的事件，根因是 AI 实验室在隔离（containment）与监控上的失效，而不是模型有了自己的意图。对 CISO 来说，重点应放在审查 AI 供应商、补齐基础安全措施，而非简单地禁用 AI 工具。
items.summary_en: Cybersecurity experts say the recent alarming hacking reports blamed on AI come down to containment and monitoring failures at AI labs, not agents acting with minds of their own. For CISOs, that reframes the job as vetting AI vendors and tightening security basics rather than treating the models themselves as the threat.

items.title: Passkeys are not a trap
items.content: Passkeys Are Not a Trap Home Speaking Training Media Contact Sponsor 🌙 Subscribe Sponsored by: Report URI - Passkeys protect login, not the session. Monitor what happens after authentication. Passkeys Passkeys Are Not a Trap Scott Helme Security researcher, entrepreneur and international speaker who specialises in web technologies. More posts by Scott Helme. Scott Helme 14 Oct 2026 • 4 min read A post called Passkeys are a trap. Do not use them. has been doing the rounds over the last few days, making it pretty high on Hacker News, and I've had it sent to me many times with an 'is this true?' kind of vibe. It's written for "non-technical citizens of the web", and the headline advice is to stop using passkeys and go back to TOTP codes and passwords. The Argument The post makes what appears to be one central claim: Passkeys support something called attestation, which lets a website ask for cryptographic proof of what made the passkey. The author calls this a "hidden dial" and argues that sites will slowly turn it up, until you're only allowed to log in with approved software on an approved operating system, with no modifications, no LineageOS and no sharing your Netflix password. Throw in uBlock Origin, the FIDO Alliance membership list and the UK's image-scanning proposals, and the conclusion is that passkeys are "not designed to prioritize your interests". <that-escalated-quickly.gif> It's a compelling story. It just doesn't match how any of this actually works... Your Passkeys Don't Attest The passkeys most people use are synced passkeys, stored in iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden or whatever other software of your choosing. These passkeys don't give websites an attestation statement at all, and though a site can ask, what comes back is none . I know this because I wrote an opensource passkeys library and made it available to everyone. If a consumer website decided tomorrow that it would only accept attested passkeys, it would lock out

items.title: What I self-host
items.content: What I Self-Host | Clever Blog Title About Posts RSS What I Self-Host 2026-10-10 What I Self-Host, What I Don’t, and Why I’ve always had a foot in the self-hosting world, long before it was called that. My freshman year of university, I ran a website from a Linux box underneath my bed. There was some downtime when my roommate got tired of the fan noise and turned it off. For several years I ran MythTV , then XBMC (later known as Kodi). Recently, I lived for a few years in India, where streaming services are extremely inexpensive by western standards. We had Netflix, Disney Plus (Hotstar in India), and Spotify. After leaving India, I was unwilling to pay western prices for these services. But I had also become fed up with the engagement treadmill, particularly for my son. We wanted to limit his viewing choices to certain programming, but the constant “recommended for you” and “up next” caused conflict. While there are ways to limit content to specific titles, or disable auto-play, doing this for each service and keeping track of when client applications change and need to be reconfigured is too much work. So, I “cut the cord” in a different sense, ditching streaming services for self-hosted Jellyfin . Over the course of the next year and a half, Jellyfin opened the door to self-hosting many other services, reducing my dependence on cloud service providers, and providing a welcome stability. No longer am I constantly confronted with unnecessary site redesigns, new features of questionable value, and a barrage of e-mails about terms-of-service updates, binding arbitration, data breaches, etc. I read the release notes of new versions of the software I host and decide if and when I want to upgrade. Rules I have a few ground rules. With the exception of VPN servers that run on my router, I do not expose any services directly to the public internet. items.title: Show HN: Petal, open-source CoScreen/ScreenHero finally free
items.content: Hi HN! I’m Jason Thomas, one of the founders of CoScreen. As some of you may know, Datadog sunset the CoScreen service on July 31st. Four of us from the original CoScreen team have spent the last couple months building a free and open source pair programming tool inspired by those that came before us: It’s called Petal ( https://github.com/kiruna-labs/petal ) Some history first, because when we started CoScreen we had hoped to break the sad and established pattern of this industry. Screenhero was an exceptional tool that a lot of us loved for pairing. Multiple cursors, low latency, you could click your partner’s editor, and just start typing. It felt like magic while we had it. Then Slack bought it in 2015, and shut down the standalone app in December 2017. When Till, Max, and I started CoScreen, we were aware of this history, and wanted to build an even more magical collaboration and screen sharing experience: the entire concept was “throw a window from your laptop up on someone else’s screen, and start collaborating with zero friction.” Datadog acquired us in 2022, and thus began the great adventure of adapting our real-time technology into Datadog products, while also continue developing CoScreen as a standalone tool from the Datadog ecosystem. Datadog invested in the product for years and we’re thankful for that. But CoScreen itself proved, like so many other screen sharing tool acquisitions, to be too tangential from the customer base and core mission. We instead built other communication features in Datadog, the integrations with other video platforms, and also its wildly successful MCP server. We weren't the only ones. Around was bought by Miro and shut down in March 2025. Multi (formerly Remotion) was acqui-hired by OpenAI in 2024 and shut down about a month later. It's nearly always the same story: a small team builds something hard that people love, a platform buys it for the team or the feature, and the standalone product doesn't survive the integration.

items.title: Show HN: Wonderhop – A daily game: guess what most people say, or what none do
items.content: Hello HN! Wonderhop is a small browser game with no account needed to play, everyday there are 4 rounds of 7 quesitons like "Name a food that a lot of people hate" The goal depends on the mode: Either gives the answer most people would give, the one no one would give, the oldest answer or the most recent one and there's a leaderboard for the day. The most interesting part of the project was understanding answers that are typed freely and in 10 languages, there was some typos, plurals, nickname, or even duplicate way of sayign the same thing. We needed AI judge that checks it really existes conencted to some API like wikipedia to judge the veracity of each answer really quickly (less than 1s on average) The percentage starts from an estimate but move really fast with the answers of real players. If the list missed a good answer, it gets added as soon as a few different players give it. (There are also a lot of secrets and pop culture references added in the game :) ) A large part of the code was written with AI tools, but the artistic direction the concept and every choice design are human-made We'd love to know if the goal is clear from the very first question while playing and were any good answers rejected unfairly We are a couple of developers from Montreal that like guessing games so we built this in about two month. Thanks a lot!

items.title: Show HN: Stoke Money – Personal finance app built around a cash flow forecast
items.content: Hi HN, I've been through many finance tracking apps, starting with Personal Capital, then Monarch, and most recently Copilot. None of them have worked perfectly for my needs. All of these apps tend to model “cash flow” as the net sum of your transactions during a month, yet while credit card charges are reported immediately, they are typically deducted from checking (cash) accounts the following month when the bill is due. As a result, I've always had to maintain a separate spreadsheet to track my actual cash flow. These apps also have a huge focus on managing budgets, which has never been for me. My spending is rarely consistent month-to-month, so every month I'm comparing my fully justified spending against my budget, and tweaking my budget until I “pass”. So I built yet another finance tracking app. It has the usual components - accounts, transactions, categories - but the core is a cash flow projection engine, and everything else is built around it. Budgets are gone. Instead, each income/spending category is projected forward from your historical activity, but not as a flat monthly number. They land in whatever account you historically use (e.g. checking account for paychecks/rent/bills, credit/debit cards for daily spending). Credit card payments are modeled automatically based on your projected credit card balance. You can set up your own recurring transfers between accounts as well, to model savings, for example. The end result is that the app can forecast how your cash moves, and you can see in advance when any account might run low. If all of your accounts look good for the next 12 months, maybe you don't have a budgeting problem. What’s made the biggest difference for me has been the MCP integration, which I have connected to Claude (but can be connected to any AI agent of your choice). items.title: Show HN: MirrorMD – An AI second opinion from a facial cosmetic surgeon
items.content: Hi HN, I am a facial cosmetic surgeon and have been practicing for just over 20 years. I work in Beverly Hills and Miami and my practice is both surgical and non-surgical (ie fillers) and I specialize in very natural results. I always tell patients: the procedures are easy to do but making it look natural is the hard part. I am constantly surprised at the interactions I have with patients who don't have the experience to know when another provider is selling them on treatments that I know either don't work or can even cause harm long-term. I also realize I can only serve 1 patient at a time. I wanted to try democratize the consultation experience and give patients the information needed to make an informed decision based upon the published literature and my own clinical experience. The website I created is called MyMirrorMD.com and is designed to help patients know what treatments would be supported for their unique face, in what volumes/amount and approximate price points. I've also added a section called "guide" that compares common treatments and answers many of the questions I have fielded day after day for many years. Would love to know your feedback on this project, which is my first foray into using AI and building a website!

# Claude Code Plugins Directory

A curated directory of high-quality plugins for Claude Code.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins from partners and the community

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Internal Plugins

Internal plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation.

### External Plugins

Third-party partners can submit plugins for inclusion in the marketplace. External plugins must meet quality and security standards for approval. To submit a new plugin, use the [plugin directory submission form](https://clau.de/plugin-directory-submission).

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

# AI Job Search *The job search that runs on your machine.*

[![CI](https://github.com/MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search/actions/workflows/ci.yml) An AI-powered job application framework built on [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). Fork it, fill in your profile, and let Claude evaluate job postings, tailor your CV, write cover letters, and prepare you for interviews. > Note: This is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or maintained by Anthropic. Anthropic and Claude Code are referenced only to describe the toolchain this workflow uses. > > This project has **no affiliated cryptocurrency, token, or paid sponsorship program**. Anything claiming otherwise is unauthorized and should be treated as a scam. The only ways to support the project are the Ko-fi link below and contributing on GitHub. ## Does it actually work? I'm a geophysicist by training. When my position was cut in late 2025, I built this framework to run my own job search - the same `/scrape`, `/apply`, and `/interview` workflow in this repo, used weekly, on my own career. I was upfront about it with every employer I spoke to, and instead of counting against me, it usually sparked a genuine technical conversation. Sixty-nine tailored applications, twenty first interviews, and one signed contract later, I started as an AI engineer in June 2026. People kept asking whether this actually works.

items.title: android/skills
items.readme:
## Android skills

**Android skills** are a dedicated repository of **AI-optimized, modular instructions** and
resources, to help agents better understand and execute specific patterns that follow the best
practices and guidance on Android development
from [developer.android.com](https://developer.android.com).

Android skills follow the [open-standard agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) - markdown
files (SKILL.md) that provide a technical specification of a task, and **ground LLMs** with
information on specialized domains and workflows.

Our Android skill development focuses on **use cases and workflows where evaluations show LLMs
underperform**.
We aren't prioritizing well-established areas where LLMs are already proficient, such
as basic Jetpack Compose best practices.

To learn more, read the official documentation:

- [Android skills](https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-skills)
- [Android CLI](https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-cli)
- [Android Studio](https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/skills)

### Install Android skills

Use Android CLI to install a specific skill into the current directory:

```
android skills add r8-analyzer --project=.
```

Use Android CLI to install all Android skills to directories for all detected agents:

```
android skills add --all
```

If you don't have any existing agent directories and don't specify particular agents, the skills
will be installed for Gemini and Antigravity at `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills`.

**Options:**

- `--all` - Add all Android skills. If omitted, only the `android-cli` skill will be installed.
- `--agent` - A comma-separated list of agents to install the skill for. If omitted, the skill will be installed for all detected agents.
- `--project` - Path to a project root in which to install the skills.


To update all skills or specific ones, run:

```
android skills update --all
android skills update wear-compose-m3
```

### Install as an agent plugin

items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
items.readme:
# security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and fin

These agents draft analyst work product — models, memos, research notes, reconciliations — for review by a qualified professional. They do not make investment recommendations, execute transactions, bind risk, post to a ledger, or approve onboarding; every output is staged for human sign-off. You are responsible for verifying outputs and for compliance with the laws and regulations that apply to your firm.

What's in the repo:

- **[Agents](#agents)** — named, end-to-end workflow agents (Pitch Agent, Market Researcher, GL Reconciler, …). Each ships as a Cowork plugin **and** as a [Claude Managed Agent template](./managed-agent-cookbooks) you deploy via `/v1/agents`.
- **[Vertical plugins](#vertical-plugins)** — the underlying skills, slash commands, and data connectors, bundled by FSI vertical. Install these on their own if you just want `/comps`, `/dcf`, `/earnings` and the connectors without a full agent.

## Agents

Each agent is named for the workflow it runs. They're starting points: install the ones that match your work, then tune the prompts, skills, and connectors to how your firm does it.

Each agent plugin is **self-contained** — it bundles the skills it uses, so installing the agent is all you need.

items.readme:
# Agent Substrate **Zero-trust sandboxing for millions of agents on Kubernetes.** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [Quickstart](#quickstart-development) · [Security](docs/security.md) · [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
## What is Agent Substrate? Agent Substrate is a security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. Purpose-built for the era of autonomous agents, Substrate delivers fast resume operations in less than 400ms, with more than 1500 activations per second. Agents get isolated compute, identity, networking, and storage. Sensitive credentials are kept out of reach from untrusted code. It supports multiple sandbox technologies, including microVMs and gVisor, while enabling a consistent lifecycle and management of all sandboxes. At its core, Agent Substrate maps a larger set of “actors” (stateful workloads such as agents) onto a smaller pool of ready “workers”. Because agents spend most of their lives waiting on models, tools, or humans, Substrate snapshots idle actors out of memory and restores them when a request arrives. Substrate is a low-opinion runtime, not an agent SDK. The workloads it runs do not have to be AI agents, though autonomous, untrusted, mostly-idle agents are the target for its isolation and scheduling model. It runs on standard Kubernetes: Pods, autoscaling, NetworkPolicies. It adds agent-specific scheduling, snapshotting, identity, and network mediation. This allows agentic, inference, training, and reinforcement learning workloads

items.readme: # Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the [National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components and/or scripts using Java or Python. In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential vulnerabilities in networks and systems. If you are a U.S. citizen interested in projects like this, to develop Ghidra and other cybersecurity tools for NSA to help protect our nation and its allies, consider applying for a [career with us][career]. ## Security Warning **WARNING:** There are known security vulnerabilities within certain versions of Ghidra. items.title: Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
items.description: Cursor 让我第一次强烈感受到 AI 编程的震撼，Codex 则让我第一次真正感觉到，AI 不只是编程助手，而是一个真正的超级Agent，Codex 明显更接近下一阶段的形态。
items.summary_zh: 这是一篇掘金文章，作者记录了自己从 Cursor 切换到 Codex、持续使用大半个月后的真实体验。在他看来，Cursor 让他第一次强烈感受到 AI 编程的价值，而 Codex 更像一个能自主完成任务的超级 Agent，而不只是编程助手，形态更接近下一阶段。适合正在做 AI 编程工具选型的开发者。
items.summary_en: A Juejin post by a developer who switched from Cursor to Codex and has used it for roughly half a month. Cursor, the author says, was his first strong taste of what AI coding can do, while Codex feels less like a coding assistant and more like an autonomous super-agent, closer to the next stage of tooling. Useful for developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt.

items.title: 公司从 400 多人缩减到 100 多人，我开始重新思考程序员的未来
items.description: 35岁的程序员，是不是已经落幕了？ 最近一直在逛掘金的文章，有技术文章，有人生感悟，还有各种沸点。 看得越多，越觉得现在大家都不容易。 大环境的影响，加上 AI 的冲击，感觉整个行业正在进入一个落幕阶
items.summary_zh: 掘金上的一篇个人随笔，作者所在公司从 400 多人缩减到 100 多人，他借此重新思考程序员的未来，文中还提到 35 岁程序员的处境以及大环境和 AI 冲击带来的失落感。它不是技术教程，而是从业者对行业收缩期的观察，适合正在考虑职业规划的人读。
items.summary_en: A personal essay on Juejin whose author watched their company shrink from over 400 people to just over 100, and uses that to rethink the future of programmers, touching on the situation of 35-year-old developers and the combined pressure of a weak market and AI. It is not a technical tutorial but one developer's read on an industry in retreat, useful for anyone weighing career plans.

items.title: 从codex转战workbuddy使用一周的感受
items.description: 不是恰饭，也不是踩一捧一。只是记录一个 Codex 老用户切换到 WorkBuddy 的真实一周，以及过程中踩到的坑和省下的钱。 一、为什么换：被逼无奈的"搬家" 很早就听说腾讯出了智能体编程工具 W
items.summary_zh: 一位 Codex 老用户记录了自己切换到腾讯智能体编程工具 WorkBuddy 一周的真实体验，包括过程中踩到的坑和省下的钱，并强调既非恰饭也不踩一捧一。对于正在纠结 AI 编程工具选型、关心迁移成本与实际开销的开发者，这类一线对比比官方宣传更有参考价值。
items.summary_en: A long-time Codex user documents a week of switching to WorkBuddy, Tencent's agentic coding tool, covering the pitfalls hit along the way and the money saved. The write-up is explicitly not sponsored and avoids trashing either tool, which makes it worth reading for developers weighing a migration and wondering what it really costs.

items.title: 太猛了，一个月干到15W+，给大家推荐一个最近爆火的开源逆向工具：REA
items.description: 最近 AI 圈里爆火的一个开源项目：REA，今年 4 月才建仓，目前已经干到了 15 万+ star，严格来说，是最近一个多月直接冲到了15W+ star，相信很多人应该都听说过这个项目了...

items.title: 🚀 2026 年 9 月 GitHub 十大热门项目排行榜 🔥
items.description: 欢迎来到 2026 年 9 月 GitHub 热门开源项目排行榜！它们共同指向：Agent 正在从「会写很多代码」走向更克制、更可治理、更能操作真实世界与组织协作。

items.title: 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
items.description: 先说一个事实：2026 年的技术面试，已经和两年前完全不一样了。两年前面试问的是："手写一个 Promise"、"说说 React Fiber 原理"...现在面试官默认你会用 AI。他们真正想知道的
items.summary_zh: 这篇掘金文章讨论 2026 年技术面试的变化：两年前还在考手写 Promise、React Fiber 原理，如今面试官默认候选人会用 AI，转而追问「AI 能写 80% 的代码，公司为什么还需要你」。文章要回答的正是开发者该展示哪些 AI 替代不了的判断力和工程能力，适合正在准备面试的工程师。
items.summary_en: A Juejin post on how 2026 technical interviews differ from two years ago: instead of hand-writing a Promise or explaining React Fiber, interviewers now assume candidates already use AI and ask why a company should still hire them when AI writes 80% of the code. It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

items.title: AI会让程序员失业吗？200年前的手工织工已经给出了答案
items.description: 1800年前后，一个英国手工织工坐在家里。 他的脚踩着织机，手一下一下推动梭子。 这台机器不漂亮，也不先进。 但它是他的饭碗。 他的价值，就藏在这双手里。 然而，有一天，工厂里出现了一种织布机器，它不
items.summary_zh: 文章从1800年前后一名英国手工织工讲起：他靠脚踏织机、手推梭子维生，价值全在一双手上，直到工厂里出现了新的织布机器。作者用这段历史类比当下 AI 对程序员的冲击，讨论技术替代与技能贬值。适合关心 AI 对职业前景影响的开发者阅读。
items.summary_en: The piece opens with an English handloom weaver around 1800, who made his living by foot and shuttle until a weaving machine appeared in the factory. It uses that history as a parallel for how AI may reshape programmers' work, asking what happens when a skill stops being the thing that pays. Aimed at developers weighing AI's effect on their careers.

items.title: 用了一个月 WorkBuddy，聊聊我的真实感受
items.description: 我用 GPT 有两年多了，也算是个重度用户了吧。平常写方案、改文案、整理资料、有时候半夜想到一个选题也会爬起来跟它聊两轮。因为网络的原因，我一直走的是中转站——大家懂的都懂，就是第三方转发 API 的
items.summary_zh: 一位用 GPT 两年多的重度用户，记录自己连续用了一个月 WorkBuddy 的真实感受；他此前因为网络原因，一直通过第三方中转 API 调用 GPT。文中结合写方案、改文案、整理资料等日常场景给出评价，适合正在挑 AI 工具的人参考。
items.summary_en: A heavy GPT user of more than two years, who had been calling the API through a third-party relay because of network issues, writes up his impressions after a month with WorkBuddy. The piece works through everyday tasks such as drafting proposals, editing copy and organizing materials, so it is aimed at people comparing AI tools for daily work.

items.title: AI 时代，软件程序员未来 10—15 年的职业前景
items.description: 软件开发不会消失，但以“编写代码”为主要价值的程序员，将面临持续的职业价值重估。未来可能需要更多软件，却不一定需要同比例增长的程序员。

items.title: 基于 Pi，我居然自己搞了一个好用的 AI Agent 桌面工作台
items.description: 先说结论：别重复造轮子 很多人一听"自己开发 Agent"，第一反应是"那不得从模型调用、消息循环、工具协议、权限系统一路手写？"。 其实不用。Ag
items.summary_zh: 这篇掘金文章的作者基于 Pi 搭了一个自用的 AI Agent 桌面工作台，核心主张是不要重复造轮子：模型调用、消息循环、工具协议、权限系统这些环节不必从零手写。它适合想自己动手做 Agent 桌面工具的开发者，重点在于如何复用已有能力，把精力放在工作台本身。
items.summary_en: A Juejin post describes how the author built an AI Agent desktop workbench on top of Pi. Its main argument is not to reinvent the wheel: the model calls, message loop, tool protocol and permission system do not need to be written from scratch. It is aimed at developers who want their own agent desktop tool without rebuilding the plumbing first.

items.title: 甲方只给了一张卫星截图，我用 Three.js + Blender 建了一座 3D 能源站
items.description: 一张卫星截图，用 Three.js + Blender 建出一座 3D 综合能源补给站：反求设计稿相机、脚本化建模、Cycles 烘焙夜景、重卡倒车入位、运营仿真，再用叠图逐像素校验还原度。
items.summary_zh: 作者只拿到一张卫星截图，就用 Three.js 加 Blender 建出一座 3D 综合能源补给站：反求设计稿相机、脚本化建模、Cycles 烘焙夜景、重卡倒车入位与运营仿真，最后用叠图逐像素校验还原度。适合想看 3D 重建和图形管线实操细节的开发者。
items.summary_en: Working from just one satellite screenshot, the author rebuilt a 3D integrated energy station with Three.js and Blender: reverse-engineering the design camera, scripting the model, baking a night scene in Cycles, animating a heavy truck backing into place, running an operations simulation, and checking fidelity pixel by pixel with overlays. Worth reading if you care about 3D reconstruction and graphics pipeline practice.

items.title: 每天白嫖 WorkBuddy 100 积分，我让WorkBuddy自己领
items.description: 有没有小伙伴跟我一样，每天都去白嫖 WorkBuddy 的 100 积分，每天都怕忘记领。 其实我早就开了会员，但还是会有积分焦虑，天天惦记着今天的积分领没领。
items.summary_zh: 一位开发者写了篇记录，讲怎么让 WorkBuddy 自己把每天的 100 免费积分领掉，不用再手动惦记。作者说自己早就开了会员，但依然有积分焦虑，于是干脆把领取动作自动化。同样的 WorkBuddy 用户可以直接参考这套做法。
items.summary_en: A developer documented how to automate WorkBuddy's daily 100 free credits so the app claims them on its own instead of needing a manual check-in. The author notes they already pay for a membership yet still felt anxious about missing a day, which is what pushed them to automate it. Anyone using WorkBuddy who keeps forgetting the daily claim can follow the same approach.

items.title: 这个本地模型，让我 token 自由了
items.description: Qwen3.8-27B 把旗舰级 Agent 能力搬进个人电脑，本地运行不花 API 费用，但速度、内存和长任务体验仍有明显门槛。
items.summary_zh: 掘金这篇文章讲的是 Qwen3.8-27B，一个能跑在个人电脑上、不花 API 费用的本地模型，主打把旗舰级 Agent 能力搬到本机。作者也点明代价：速度、内存占用和长任务体验仍有明显门槛，适合愿意折腾本地推理、对响应速度不那么敏感的人。
items.summary_en: The post looks at Qwen3.8-27B, a local model that brings flagship-level agent capability to a personal machine without paying API fees. The author is upfront about the trade-offs: inference speed, memory footprint and long-task experience remain real barriers. It suits developers willing to run local inference who can live with slower responses.

items.title: 😭 Electron 麻了，Deno 直接支持二进制应用，无需第三方桌面应用框架！
items.description: Deno 2.9 支持桌面应用开发，基于前端框架项目即可转化为独立的原生二进制桌面应用，无需使用 Electron 或 Tauri 等桌面应用框架，不支持移动应用，但支持交叉编译到五大平台。
items.summary_zh: Deno 2.9 开始支持桌面应用开发，前端框架项目可以直接编译成独立的原生二进制桌面程序，不再需要 Electron 或 Tauri 这类第三方框架。它支持交叉编译到五大平台但不覆盖移动端，适合想用一套前端代码换取更小分发体积、更少运行时依赖的团队先做小范围试点。
items.summary_en: Deno 2.9 adds desktop app support: a frontend-framework project can be compiled into a standalone native binary without Electron or Tauri. Cross-compilation covers five platforms, though mobile is not supported. Worth trialing for teams that want a smaller distribution footprint and fewer runtime dependencies than a full Electron stack.

Akka 在 65 个开源项目中测试基于规格的 AI 交付
items.content: Akka 利用 65 个开源项目，对一种基于规格说明的 AI 辅助软件移植工作流进行了 测试 ，评估内容包括：规格说明的结构、上下文、模型和工作量选择、自动化验证、token 消耗以及运行时性能。首轮测试耗时 99.3 小时，消耗了 94.1 亿个令牌。根据 Akka 的报告，在 65 个移植项目中，有 57 个在代码行数或性能方面实现了提升。 该实验分成了两个阶段。 Akka 对全部 65 个项目进行了分析，生成规格说明并实现了每个项目最多 10% 的功能。随后，他们根据系统特性和可量化的结果，从中选出 10 个项目进行了完整实现。交付管控工作流循环经历了需求发现、规格定义、移植、基准测试和优化等阶段。需求发现阶段对代码、模型、模式和运行时行为进行了分析，而 Claude 配合 Akka Specify 则负责实现、测试和审查工作，然后通过一个通用的基准测试运行器，对测试、代码规模和延迟进行了比较。 Akka 发现，包含声明、证据和类型化行为的结构化规格说明能够改善首次实现的效果，而上下文文件中缺少了跨组件决策的内容。后续研究领域包括接口枚举、测试数据导入、溯源追踪、差异测试和对抗性测试。 GitHub Spec Kit 同样围绕规格说明、规划、任务、实现和收敛这几个环节，对编码代理的工作流进行了结构化设计。在 Akka 的实验中，Sonnet 平均每项移植耗时 61 分钟，而 Opus 则为 120 分钟；但 Opus 的 token 消耗量少了大约 40%。虽然提高工作量设置会增加消耗，却并不能获得持续的效率提升。 研究结果的发布引发了工程师们的一番讨论。在 LinkedIn 上， Aaditya 在 Akka 首席执行官 Tyler Jewell 的一篇博文下 评论 道： 规模较小的模型其行为与他观察到的现代化改造工作相符，即较小的模型会严格遵循规范，而较大的模型则可能会进行即兴调整。 Aaditya 还提出了一个 问题 ： 代码行数的减少主要是源于死代码的移除，还是源于目标语言的差异？ 在同一场讨论中，Avahi 市场部负责人 Rick Bryce 提到 了一个相关的点，并指出限制条件可能会影响结果。这些评论引发了新的疑问：移植效率的差异究竟是源于模型能力、规格限制，还是两者兼而有之。 成本更低的模型能实现更精确的移植，这一发现值得深入探究。 验证工作采用了原始的单元测试和集成测试，并且同时由审核人员对序列化、安全性、错误处理、个人身份信息（PII）、幂等性以及架构边界进行了检查。随着移植故障暴露出的新问题，Akka 增加了防护措施，但同时也指出，额外的退出条件增加了移植成本。性能表现因项目而异：应用程序、框架和库的性能普遍得到提升，而基础设施和工具的性能中位数则有所下降。根据 Akka 的报告， Dify 的性能提升了 143333 倍，不过所对比的工作负载存在差异；而 Netflix Metaflow 的运行速度则慢了约 100 倍。 原文链接： https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-spec-driven-delivery/

Relevant for teams weighing AI-assisted large-scale code migration.

items.title: The World Is Not a Dataset - Building AI Systems That Continuously Learn from Reality｜QCon上海
items.content: 从「构建 AI」到「驾驭 AI」，100+ 实战案例拆解 AI Native 时代的工程新实践！ 2026 年 QCon 全球软件开发大会大会 · 上海站 将于 10 月 22 日-24 日 举办，来自阿里巴巴、腾讯、字节跳动、美团、小红书、蚂蚁集团、无问芯穹、阶跃星辰、快手、百度、网易、微软、华为、携程、平安等企业的一线技术实践者，将从 AI 应用、Agent 工程、AI Coding、基础设施、数据系统、质量、安全、SRE 以及具身智能等方向，分享 AI 进入真实生产环境之后正在发生的变化。 蚂蚁灵波科技首席数据科学家黄用韬博士已确认出席 “ 数据驱动的具身智能：迈向规模化之路 ” 专题，并发表题为 《 The World Is Not a Dataset - Building AI Systems That Continuously Learn from Reality 》 的主题分享。今天的 AI 越来越强调持续学习、自我改进和闭环迭代，但真实世界并不是一份预先准备好的数据集。对机器人而言，真正重要的不只是“拿什么数据训练”，而是如何理解数据产生时的任务、环境、硬件、模型版本与人工介入，如何从真实执行中识别能力缺口，并进一步决定下一轮该采什么、在哪里采、由谁执行，以及如何验证一次改进是否真正有效。 黄用韬博士本次分享将介绍一种面向真实世界学习的系统视角：把任务、事件、状态、数据和资源组织在持续演化的时间轴上，通过端、边、云协同，把问题发现、数据产生、模型学习、评测验证和下一次行动连接成闭环。最终，数据集不再是系统的起点和终点，而是持续学习过程中动态形成的一种结果。 黄用韬博士，本科毕业于清华大学数理基础科学班，博士毕业于德州大学达拉斯分校，长期从事 AI 基础设施与分布式系统研究与实践，在自动驾驶领域拥有多年产业经验，曾任元戎启行技术合伙人，主导构建了大规模数据与训练基础设施体系，现任蚂蚁灵波科技首席数据科学家。他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下： 演讲提纲： 1. 真实世界不是一份数据集 为什么机器人学习不能只围绕静态数据集展开，以及数据集视角天然会丢失哪些关键上下文。 从数据走向事件与上下文：任务创建、机器人执行、人工介入、失败、换件、标定、模型发布，本质上都属于学习系统的一部分。 2. 学习并不是从训练开始的 模型评测发现能力缺口后，需要进一步反向决定下一轮“由谁、在哪里、采什么、如何验证”。 一次失败，不一定意味着再训练一次。失败可能来自模型能力，也可能来自硬件、环境、标定、数据质量或人工介入。 系统需要先理解反馈，再决定下一步行动。 3. 从数据流水线走向学习系统 端、边、云不只是数据传输链路，而是一个能够协同处理问题、组织资源和驱动下一轮行动的系统。 4. 持续学习真正需要什么 核心不是单纯增加数据或扩大模型，而是缩短“发现问题—获得证据—产生改进—验证改进”的完整周期 数据集不再是系统的起点和终点，而是持续学习过程中动态形成的一种结果。 实践痛点： 机器人学习若只围绕静态数据集展开，就会天然丢失任务、环境、硬件、模型版本与人工介入等关键上下文。 学习若从训练而不是从评测发现能力缺口开始，就难以反向决定下一轮由谁、在哪里、采什么、如何验证。 把一次失败简单归因于“再训练一次”，会忽略模型能力、硬件、环境、标定、数据质量或人工介入等真实原因。 端、边、云若只是数据传输链路而不能协同处理问题、组织资源和驱动下一轮行动，就无法缩短“发现问题—获得证据—产生改进—验证改进”的完整周期。 前沿亮点： 提出“真实世界不是一份数据集”的系统视角，把任务、事件、状态、数据和资源组织在持续演化的时间轴上。 重新定义学习起点，主张学习并不是从训练开始，而是从模型评测发现能力缺口、理解反馈开始。 将端、边、云从数据流水线升级为协同处理问题、组织资源和驱动下一轮行动的学习系统。 重新定义数据集与核心指标，让数据集成为持续学习过程中动态形成的结果，并以缩短“发现问题—获得证据—产生改进—验证改进”周期为目标。 听众收益 ： 理解为什么机器人学习不能只围绕静态数据集展开，以及数据集视角会丢失哪些关键上下文。 掌握把任务、事件、状态、数据和资源组织在持续演化时间轴上的真实世界学习系统视角。 学会从真实执行中识别能力缺口，并反向决定下一轮“由谁、在哪里、采什么、如何验证”。 获得失败归因与闭环度量框架，能够以缩短“发现问题—获得证据—产生改进—验证改进”周期来重新审视自身系统。 除此之外，本次大会还策划了 Loop Engineering 、 千行百业 Agent 创新实践 、 Agent 自主进化：从记忆到持续学习 、 Agent as a Service 、 Vibe Coding 时代的新质量债 、 理性驾驭 AI 的 SRE 可靠性工
items.summary_zh: 蚂蚁灵波科技首席数据科学家黄用韬将在 10 月 22-24 日的 QCon 上海站分享《The World Is Not a Dataset》，指出机器人学习不能只围绕静态数据集，任务创建、人工介入、失败与标定等上下文都属学习系统的一部分。他主张以端、边、云协同把问题发现、数据产生、模型学习与评测串成闭环，让数据集成为持续学习的结果而非起点。
items.summary_en: At QCon Shanghai (October 22-24), Huang Yongtao, chief data scientist at Ant Lingbo Technology and a former tech partner at DeepRoute.ai, will argue in "The World Is Not a Dataset" that robot learning cannot be built around static datasets, since task setup, human intervention, failures and recalibration are all part of the learning system. He proposes an end-edge-cloud loop linking problem discovery, data collection, training and evaluation, so datasets become an output of continual learning rather than its starting point.

items.title: Java 近期新闻：JobRunr 9、OpenXava 8、Quarkus、LangChain4j、JNoSQL、Lathe
items.content: OpenJDK JEP 544（ 提前代码编译 ）已经从 Proposed to Target 状态 提升 至 Targeted 状态，并计划在 JDK 28 中交付。该 JEP 旨在缩短应用程序的启动和预热时间，使应用程序在 HotSpot JVM 启动时就可以立即使用经过优化的原生代码。这样，应用程序就能够更快地达到峰值性能，并保持这一性能水平。 JDK 28 JDK 28 的 早期访问构建 Build 18 发布，它是 Build 17 的 升级 ，修复了各种 问题 。要了解关于这个构建的更多细节，请参阅 发布说明 。 对于 JDK 28 ，欢迎开发者通过 Java Bug 数据库 报告 Bug。 Jakarta EE 在每周博客 Hashtag Jakarta EE 中，Eclipse 基金会 Jakarta EE 开发大使 Ivar Grimstad 介绍了 Jakarta EE 12 的最新进展 ，他写道： 关于 Jakarta EE 12，目前正在就将 Jakarta Authorization 纳入 Jakarta EE Web Profile 进行投票。将它与 Web Profile 中的其他安全规范归为一类是完全合理的。应指导委员会的要求，他们本周在平台电话会议上讨论并敲定了 Jakarta EE 12 的时间表。Jakarta EE 12 的时间表如下： - 12 月 1 日 — Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile - 3 月 31 日 — Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile - 5 月 15 日 — Jakarta EE 12 Platform 就我个人而言，我非常希望 Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile 能纳入 Jakarta NoSQL 这一规范。在将人工智能集成到企业应用程序时，简化和标准化对 NoSQL 数据存储的访问是一项非常有用的功能。特别是对 RAG 向量数据库的支持，将非常实用。如果你赞同我的观点，或者对将 Jakarta NoSQL 纳入 Jakarta EE 12 有任何看法，请务必通过电子邮件列表或平台电话会议告诉我们。社区的声音至关重要！ 最近， Eclipse JNoSQL （Jakarta NoSQL 的兼容实现）已经从孵化项目晋升为 Eclipse Enterprise for Java（EE4J）项目。该项目自 2017 年起便已经成为 Eclipse 项目，并自 Jakarta EE 11 起作为 Jakarta Data 支持的一部分被纳入了 Eclipse GlassFish 。 JobRunr JobRunr 9.0.0 发布 ，带来了以下值得注意的变化：仪表盘的历史记录部分新增了一个 Chart 选项卡，以甘特图的形式展示任务的生命周期，其中，每种状态和每个持久化步骤各占一行；支持 Micronaut 5 和 Quarkus 3.40；当序列化任务过大时，系统会触发警告， 抛出 StepExecutionException 异常并解包。要了解有关该版本的更多详情，请参阅 发布说明 以及观看 9.0 版本发布时的网络研讨会 。InfoQ 随后将发布一篇更详细的新闻报道。 OpenXava OpenXava 8.0.0 版本 发布 ，带来了 Bug 修复、文档改进、依赖项升级以及以下新功能：基于 Spring Boot 构建的 OpenXava；对 Jakarta EE 11 规范的部分支持；更现代化的界面风格。要了解有关该版本的更多详情，请参阅 发布说明 。 Quarkus Quarkus 3.34.0 发布 ，带来了一些 Bug 修复和值得注意的变更，包括：改进了 AeshLauncher 接口，使其信号协议和超时诊断更加稳健；消除了 ResteasyReactiveJacksonProcessor 类在端点返回 void 时产生的不必要的警告。要了解有关该版本的更多详情，请参阅 3.40.1 和 3.40.0 版本的发布说明。 Micronaut Micronaut 基金会 发布 了基于 Micronaut Core 5.2.11 和 5.2.8 的 Micronaut Framework 5.2.1 和 5.2.0 版本（发布公告分别见 这里 和 这里 ）。除修复了 Bug 并更新了 Micronaut 生态系统中的许多模块外，还包括以下新功能：对 Micronaut for Python 的实验性支持，用于在编译时处理 Python 源代码；新增一个 Micronaut Jakarta EL 模块，实现了 Jakarta 表达式语言 规范。要了解有关该版本的更多详情，请参阅 5.2.1 和 5.2.0 版本

items.summary_en: OpenJDK's JEP 544, ahead-of-time code compilation, has moved to Targeted for delivery in JDK 28, letting applications run optimized native code as the HotSpot JVM starts and reach peak performance sooner; JDK 28 Early Access Build 18 also shipped. The roundup covers the Jakarta EE 12 schedule for each profile, Eclipse JNoSQL's promotion from incubation to an EE4J project, and JobRunr 9.0.0, which adds a Gantt-chart view of job lifecycles to its dashboard.

items.title: 聚焦 AI 场景落地与 FDE 创新，2026 人工智能产业大会专项活动在济南举行
items.content: 随着大模型和智能体加快进入企业生产经营环节，AI 应用正在从“能力可用”进一步走向“业务可交付”。围绕真实场景、工程交付和产业协同，2026 人工智能产业大会专项活动“ AI 场景落地与 FDE 创新发展交流对接活动”在济南举行，并同步启动 2027 人工智能产业大赛、共智方舟社区，发布《 2026—2027 AI 场景落地与 FDE 创新发展行动计划》。 10 月 16 日，2026 人工智能产业大会专项活动——“ AI 场景落地与 FDE 创新发展交流对接活动”在济南黄河国际会展中心举行。 随着大模型、智能体能力持续演进，企业推进 AI 应用的关注点，正从“技术能不能实现”进一步转向“场景是否值得做、如何进入业务流程、如何完成交付并持续产生价值”。 围绕这些现实问题，本次活动从企业真实需求出发，通过场景征集、案例分享、FDE 实践交流和供需对接，探索 AI 从技术能力走向业务落地的具体路径，并同步启动 2027 人工智能产业大赛、共智方舟社区，发布《 2026—2027 AI 场景落地与 FDE 创新发展行动计划》。 山东省工业和信息化厅数据产业推进处副处长、三级调研员王俊人，山东省社会组织总会党委书记、会长王安忠出席活动并致辞。 本次活动由山东省大数据协会、极客邦科技、积木网等单位举办，山东省社会组织总会支持。来自人工智能、大数据产业链企业，企业数字化转型部门、高校科研院所、社会组织及 FDE 相关领域的代表参与现场交流。 AI 落地，正从“能力可用”走向“业务可交付” 企业获得大模型和 AI 工具的门槛正在降低，但真正将 AI 嵌入生产经营流程，仍需要解决场景价值、数据基础、系统适配、组织协同和持续运营等问题。 活动现场，多位嘉宾结合企业实践展开主题分享。 山东省鲁信投资控股集团有限公司首席信息官、山东征信党委书记、董事长徐伟以《集团型企业如何推进 AI 应用——鲁信集团的探索与思考》为题，分享大型集团在推进 AI 应用过程中的实践经验；腾讯 WorkBuddy 架构师蒋萍围绕《腾讯云 WorkBuddy 核心能力及落地场景介绍》，介绍企业级智能体在实际业务中的能力边界和应用场景；山东麦港数据系统有限公司技术总监尹思杰则从“前线部署”进一步谈到“平台复用”。在《从前线部署到平台复用：麦港行业数字大脑实践分享》中，他结合行业项目实践，讨论如何将一线业务需求、解决方案和交付经验进一步沉淀为可复制的平台能力。山东省社会组织总会秘书长马光健从社会组织实际工作出发，介绍 AI 在管理与服务提效中的应用实践。 从现场分享来看，AI 落地正在从单点工具应用走向更复杂的业务系统，业务理解、系统集成、数据基础和组织协同的重要性进一步凸显。 FDE 连接技术与业务，补上 AI 落地的工程环节 在这条从模型到业务的链路中，FDE 成为本次活动反复出现的关键词。 随着 AI 应用进一步走向复杂产业场景，传统“业务提需求—产品设计—研发开发—项目交付”的长链条，容易出现需求失真、响应周期过长和技术与业务脱节等问题。 FDE 更加贴近客户和真实业务现场，需要同时理解业务问题和技术能力，并参与需求识别、方案设计、部署、联调和持续迭代。 117AI FDE 团队负责人孙斌以《共创生态，交付价值—— FDE 助力企业智能化转型》为题，围绕 FDE 如何推动企业智能化项目从需求走向交付展开分享；中关村人才协会 FDE 人才发展智库专家陈阳在《从能力标准到场景交付：FDE 人才培养的实践路径》中，围绕 FDE 人才需要具备哪些能力、如何从标准走向真实场景交付进行分享。 与此同时，AI 真正进入企业生产和业务系统后，安全也不再只是外围问题。西安四叶草信息技术有限公司安全咨询顾问霍光围绕《面向 AI 落地场景及 FDE 场景的落地安全体系保障》，从安全治理角度讨论 AI 落地过程中的风险与保障机制。 从交付实践、人才标准到安全体系，现场对 FDE 的讨论进一步延伸至 AI 落地所需的工程能力建设。 从真实需求出发，推动场景供需精准对接 本次活动将“真实场景”作为落地起点。 活动前期面向相关社会组织及会员企业征集 AI 实际应用需求，共征集来自 120 家企业/单位的 35 个应用场景，覆盖 10 多个行业/领域，涉及日常办公、会员服务、经营管理、专业服务、生产管理等方向。 在会前需求梳理基础上，会后现场进一步搭建产业对接渠道，共有 20 多家技术企业/服务机构参与交流。 后续，相关需求还将依托共智方舟社区持续跟进，推动需求梳理、技术匹配、场景验证和后续交付。 从一次论坛交流走向长期协作机制 如果说主题分享回答的是“ AI 为什么难落地、如何落地”，那么活动同步启动的产业大赛、社区和行动计划，则进一步回答了“会后如何继续”。 活动现场，2027 人工智能产业大赛
items.summary_zh: 10 月 16 日在济南举行的 2026 人工智能产业大会专项活动聚焦 AI 场景落地与 FDE（前线部署工程师）创新，现场启动 2027 人工智能产业大赛、共智方舟社区，并发布《2026—2027 AI 场景落地与 FDE 创新发展行动计划》。鲁信集团、腾讯 WorkBuddy、麦港数据等分享了集团型企业推进 AI、企业级智能体的能力边界，以及把一线交付沉淀为平台复用的做法。
items.summary_en: A special session of the 2026 AI Industry Conference in Jinan on October 16 framed the shift from "capability available" to "deliverable in business", with FDE (forward deployed engineer) practice as its center. It launched the 2027 AI industry competition and the 共智方舟 community, and released a 2026–2027 action plan for AI scenario deployment. Speakers from 鲁信集团, Tencent WorkBuddy and 麦港数据 covered enterprise-wide AI rollout and turning frontline delivery work into reusable platform capability.

items.title: 生产级大模型平台工程实战手册
items.content: 在我们将基于 LLM 的库存推荐系统投入生产运行的第一个月末，约 15% 的智能体返回结果是幻觉——听起来言之凿凿，但内容毫无事实依据。 六个月后，幻觉率降到了 1.5%。推动这一数字下降的关键，并非换用更强大的基础模型，而是我们做出的一个决定：不再将大模型相关能力视作应用层的业务问题，而是把它当作平台基础设施来对待。 本文所描述的项目，是一家大型零售企业的库存准确性平台。系统库存记录会因错放、损坏、盗窃和计数错误而与货架实际商品产生偏差，这种偏差会影响下单、补货以及商品供给。 我们的多智能体大模型系统对数百万 SKU、数十亿条历史库存记录中的异常信号进行分析，为业务方生成库存修正建议，助力业务始终保持库存数据准确。 本文描述的平台层，由业务、产品、软件工程师、数据科学家、数据工程专家共同构建，目前服务于数十个应用团队，覆盖库存审计、补货审查、差异分诊等场景。 本文记录了这次架构转型——面向企业级流量，对 Gemini、GPT 等基础模型进行统一路由与治理。下文中的这些工程范式正是我当初希望项目上线第一天就能拥有的。 文中提到的所有基础组件，都在配套的 GitHub代码库 中提供了实现，代码刻意设计为无隐藏抽象层。很多框架会用装饰器或内置智能体封装底层逻辑，而这个代码库把内部运作逻辑全部暴露，保证这些工程范式清晰易懂。 本文中的代码片段均直接取自该代码库。代码库和生产环境有一处刻意设计的差异：代码库通过 Ollama 运行本地模型 llama3.1 ，使用 LiteLLM 对接，而非调用云端托管基础模型。整个方案可以端到端本地运行，无需任何 API 费用。 为什么独立的 LLM 应用在规模化后会失效 几乎所有团队都会遇到高度相似的故障模式，甚至可以预判：原型能跑，首次生产环境部署，在一周内看起来一切正常。随后，那些评估阶段不会暴露的问题开始出现在监控面板上。 在我们的案例中，测试阶段暴露出了三类问题，每一类都是原型阶段没有覆盖到的场景。第一个是 LLM API 限流。在真实请求量下，我们开始被模型厂商限流。第二个是上下文问题。当系统推荐了不合适的商品时，根因几乎都是输入模型的数据，而非模型本身——这说明健壮的数据工程管线是解决问题的核心。第三个是大问题：幻觉。单次看很罕见，但在生产流量持续请求下，幻觉会稳定出现。我们在平台中设计了监控能力来追踪这些故障，正是这种可见性把每一个问题从谜团变成了可修复的对象。 追踪这些问题后，我们也清楚地明白：这些问题应当放在平台层统一处理，而不是交给单个应用。有三点特性尤为突出： 幻觉是输出问题，而非程序 Bug 幻觉返回的内容不会抛出调用栈异常，所有传统健康检查都能通过。下游服务接收结果并据此执行操作，很久之后才有人发现这个推荐结果对应的事实根本不存在。 Token 消耗不可控如果没有按请求归属统计用量，每月收到的账单就只有服务商给出的一行总金额。无法区分是哪个应用、哪个团队、哪个场景产生的开销，成本优化只能靠猜测。 行为不可观测延迟监控面板显示 P99 延迟正常，错误率接近 0。但模型输出质量在悄无声息地变差，但输出内容在语法上依然合法。 这些都不是应用程序的 Bug。几乎所有做大模型功能的团队都会碰到同类问题，大家第一反应都是在应用内部进行修复，于是 N 个团队写出 N 份重复的脚手架代码。这部分通用能力本应该下沉到平台层统一实现。 搭建共享大模型平台的理由 集中管理大模型能力并不是纸上谈兵。这和大型系统中集中管理 身份认证 、 日志 、 服务网格 的逻辑几乎完全一致：当多个应用存在同样的跨模块通用需求时，重复开发的成本会超过搭建共享基础设施的成本。 对 LLM 而言，共享的关注点是： 重试逻辑与故障分类 提示词注册表与版本管理 Schema 强制约束 按请求统计 Token 成本 行为可观测性 工具调用与上下文路由 跨工具服务的身份认证与授权 还有一个比重复更重要的二阶效应。共享平台强制形成契约，应用声明它们需要什么（即模型、提示词版本、Schema、工具集、评估引擎），平台负责交付。正是这种契约让新应用几天内就能上线，因为最难的部分已由平台解决。 搭建这个平台的决策点不是第一个 LLM 应用上线，而是第二个。等到十个团队都各自上线大模型功能后再在底层改造搭建平台将会是漫长艰难的迁移工作。 平台架构 图 1 展示了各个基础组件之间的组合关系。代码库实现了完整请求路径，与生产环境架构保持一致。 唯一入口是网关。网关负责调用方身份认证、签发携带角色信息的 JWT、暴露智能体执行接口、提供用户/团队维度指标、提供仅管理员可用的提示词回滚接口。网关后方，一个基于谷歌智能体开发套件 ADK 构建的根协调智能体在每一轮请求中识别意图，并将任务分发给一个或多个专家智能体；每个专家智能体绑定注册表中指定
